body:
Review-freeze trap: CRLF worktree files vs system core.autocrlf (Termal::Fable2, 2026-10-08 20:47Z; found and proven by Termal::Coder on w-48618ba39f11, TermAl mailbox 241329fa #1674-#1678).

Symptom: both reviewers of a pair STOP when they open the review. The compiled checker (`target/release/termal.exe review-freeze-check ROOT MANIFEST EXPECTED`) rejects the schema-1 literal even though the native Git endpoints (HEAD, tree, no unstaged, no untracked) look clean.

Cause: this machine sets core.autocrlf=true system-wide. Files edited on Windows can have CRLF or mixed endings in the worktree. The freeze helper ran under the inherited config, where the staged diff was 127,886 bytes; the checker's isolated settings (global=NUL, nosystem=1) read the same staged diff as 3,872,174 bytes. Adding only core.autocrlf=true to the isolated config restored the identical bytes. The checker binary wasn't the cause: the same termal.exe e92de85f failed before the normalization and passed after it.

Fix, with no Git config change: run `git ls-files --eol` on the owned paths; convert the owned files to LF (only the CR before LF removed, UTF-8 checked); stage them fully with explicit paths (no intent-to-add); show that the inherited and isolated staged diffs are byte-identical and both unstaged diffs empty (every entry i/lf w/lf); refreeze and check with the compiled checker BEFORE spawning the pair.

Prevention for implementers: before any freeze, check that `git ls-files --eol` shows w/lf for every owned path.
